title: Stop selling against the leader: how a Pune HR-tech SaaS won back its win-rate
content: SITUATION: A Pune HR-tech SaaS (payroll + compliance, ARR ~₹9 Cr, average ACV ₹1.4L) was losing 7 of every 10 competitive deals to a better-funded Bengaluru rival. Competitive win-rate had slipped from 34% to 19% over two quarters, and sales cycles stretched to 71 days because prospects ran us 'feature-by-feature' against the leader — where we always looked like the cheaper clone and discounted to stay alive. ACTION: We stopped fighting on feature parity and repositioned on the one job the rival did badly: India statutory compliance for multi-state mid-market firms (PF, ESI, PT across 12 states). We rewrote the homepage around that wedge, shipped 9 LinkedIn battlecards and a 'compliance penalty calculator', ran Google Search ads on competitor + 'compliance' intent terms (₹4.2L/quarter), and armed SDRs with a WhatsApp + email sequence that delivered each prospect's calculator result. OUTCOME: Over two quarters competitive win-rate recovered to 41%, the sales cycle fell to 52 days, and ACV rose 18% to ₹1.65L because we stopped discounting to match. Google CPL dropped from ₹1,900 to ₹1,150, and compliance-led messaging generated ₹2.3 Cr of new pipeline.
lesson: When you keep losing to one competitor, stop competing on their battlefield. Find the single segment-specific job they do badly, own it loudly across every asset, and re-frame the buyer's comparison onto your axis. The moment the deal is judged on compliance depth instead of feature count, the discount pressure disappears and ACV climbs on its own.
